source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Use reflection from two plane mirrors to decide how a simple periscope lets us see an object that is not directly visible.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Refraction at both mirrors guides the light to the observer.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: One plane mirror is enough for this Z-shaped periscope to work.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: My eye sends light through the two mirrors to the object, which lets me see it.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Yes, the periscope can see the object even when an opaque wall completely blocks its light from entering.

intelligence.enrichment: A simple periscope uses two plane mirrors in a Z-shaped box so reflection from the two mirrors enables us to see objects that are not directly visible. Each plane mirror changes the direction of light; two such reflections guide light through the periscope to the observer. The learner correctly applies this rule: A simple periscope uses two plane mirrors in a Z-shaped box so reflection from the two mirrors enables us to see objects that are not directly visible. A periscope works because the observer looks harder through a tube, not because mirrors redirect light.
